x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: Part XI was in the original Constitution; it was not added by an amendment.

st.2: Its report was reviewed by a parliamentary committee under Lal Bahadur Shastri.
st.3: The Official Languages Act ended the use of English for the official purposes of the Union from 1965.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: the Kher report was reviewed by a parliamentary committee under G.B. Pant. 3 is false: the Official Languages Act, 1963 allowed English to continue alongside Hindi after 1965.

st.4: The freedoms under Article 19 are available to citizens and foreigners alike.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: Article 19 freedoms are available only to citizens.

st.3: Its roots include the Lahore Resolution of 1940.
st.4: It bars any State aid to religious or minority institutions.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: its roots are the Karachi Resolution (1931) and the Nehru Report, not the League's Lahore Resolution. 4 is false: Indian secularism allows aid to minority institutions.

st.1: The original Preamble of 1949 described India as a 'Sovereign Socialist Democratic Republic'.
st.2: The original fraternity clause spoke of assuring 'the unity and integrity of the Nation'.

x: Statement 3 is correct. 1 is false: the original Preamble said 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'; 'Socialist' came with the 42nd Amendment. 2 is false: the original said 'unity of the Nation'; 'and integrity' was added in 1976.

st.4: Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of MP is associated with the doctrine of severability.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: Bhikaji Narain Dhakras (1955) is the leading case on the doctrine of eclipse.

st.2: Davinder Singh overruled Indra Sawhney on this point.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: Davinder Singh overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004), not Indra Sawhney.

st.2: Under the Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026, the identity certificate is issued by the National Council for Transgender Persons.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: under the 2026 amendment the District Magistrate certifies, on medical-board advice.

st.2: A Government Bill needs one month's notice and a Private Member's Bill seven days' notice.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: it is the reverse – a Government Bill needs seven days' notice and a Private Member's Bill one month's.

st.1: A joint sitting of Parliament is summoned by the President and presided over by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
st.3: Under the Second Judges Case (1993), the collegium for Supreme Court appointments consists of the CJI and the four senior-most judges.
st.4: The President addresses both Houses together at the beginning of every session of Parliament.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: a joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 3 is false: the CJI-plus-four collegium came from the Third Judges Case (1998). 4 is false: the special address is only at the first session of each year and after a general election.

st.2: Separation of powers between the executive and the legislature is a feature of India's parliamentary system.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: the parliamentary system rests on a fusion, not a separation, of the executive and the legislature.

st.1: a judge of a District Court for at least 5 years;
st.2: an advocate of a Sessions Court for at least 10 years;

x: None of the statements is correct. 1 is false: the route is 5 years as a High Court judge. 2 is false: the route is 10 years as a High Court advocate. 3 is false: the jurist must be distinguished in the opinion of the President, not the CJI.

st.2: The Governors of the member States hold the vice-chairmanship by annual rotation.
st.4: The Chief Secretaries of the member States attend as advisers with voting rights.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the Chief Ministers hold the vice-chairmanship by rotation. 4 is false: the advisers have no right to vote.

st.2: Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct and the introduction of EPIC (1993) are associated with M.S. Gill.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: strict MCC enforcement and EPIC (1993) are associated with T.N. Seshan.

st.3: Performance audit is obligatory.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: performance (efficiency) audit, like propriety audit, is discretionary.

st.1: It recommended the abolition of right to public services laws.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: it recommended enacting right to public services laws, not abolishing them.

st.4: Its Secretary-General exercises judicial powers under the Chairperson's control.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: the Secretary-General exercises administrative and financial powers, not judicial powers.

st.1: The Central Information Commission was constituted on 12 October 2005, with Satyananda Mishra as the first Chief Information Commissioner.
st.2: It came fully into force on the day of the Presidential assent.
st.4: The Rajya Sabha passed it before the Lok Sabha did.

x: Statement 3 is correct. 1 is false: the first CIC was Wajahat Habibullah. 2 is false: the Act came fully into force 120 days after assent, on 12 October 2005. 4 is false: the Lok Sabha passed it first (11 May 2005).

st.3: The coalition era since the 1990s reduced the States' say, moving away from cooperative federalism.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the coalition era gave the States a greater say and moved India towards cooperative federalism.

st.2: PAHAL is the DBT of kerosene subsidy through Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: PAHAL is the DBT of LPG subsidy, not kerosene.

st.2: Where a Ministry's majority is in doubt, the Governor's own assessment should decide it.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: Sarkaria said a doubtful majority must be tested on the floor of the House.

st.2: In INC v Institute of Social Welfare (2002), the Supreme Court held that the ECI can deregister any party for non-compliance.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: the Court held that the ECI cannot deregister a party except on narrow grounds such as fraud in registration.

st.3: Winning 6% of the votes alone, without any seat, makes a party a recognised State party.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is false: 6% of the votes qualifies only with 2 Assembly seats; votes alone need 8%.

st.3: An M2 EVM can be linked to 24 ballot units, like the M3.
st.4: M3 EVMs can record up to 3,840 votes.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the M2 takes only 4 ballot units (64 candidates). 4 is false: an M3 records up to 2,000 votes.

st.2: The CAG is the primary statutory auditor of Panchayat Raj Institutions in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the primary statutory auditor of PRIs in AP is the State Audit Department; the CAG gives technical guidance and support.

st.2: A Tribes Advisory Council consists of not more than 20 members, three-fourths of whom are ST members of the Lok Sabha from the State.
st.3: The Fifth Schedule can be amended only by a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: three-fourths of the TAC are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly. 3 is false: Parliament can amend the Fifth Schedule by ordinary law; it is not an Article 368 amendment.

st.2: Odisha has the largest ST population among the States.
st.3: No Scheduled Tribe is notified in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population. 3 is false: AP has notified STs (34 communities); no ST is notified in Punjab.

st.3: All its members are elected.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: only four-fifths of the District Planning Committee's members are elected.

st.1: The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 covers solar and wind but not pumped storage or green hydrogen.
st.2: The policy targets 160 GW of clean energy capacity, all of it from solar power.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is false: the policy also covers hybrid, pumped storage and green hydrogen/ammonia. 2 is false: its 160 GW target spans all these sources, not solar alone.

st.3: The UMANG app was part of its core infrastructure along with SWAN and State Data Centres.
st.4: It was approved with 27 Mission Mode Projects, all of them Central MMPs.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the core infrastructure was SWAN, State Data Centres and Common Service Centres, not UMANG. 4 is false: the 27 MMPs were Central, State and Integrated.

st.1: It was launched on 8 December 2023 at Praja Bhavan, Hyderabad.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: AP's Prajavani began in November 2005 in Ranga Reddy district; the 8 December 2023 Praja Bhavan launch is Telangana's Prajavani.

st.2: Krishnapatnam (Nellore) is a node of the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: Krishnapatnam is a node of the Chennai–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

st.3: It wanted social audits confined to MGNREGA.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: it wanted social audits extended to other programmes, not confined to MGNREGA.

st.2: The theory of regulatory capture, under which a regulator serves the industry it regulates rather than the public, was put forward by John Maynard Keynes.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: regulatory capture was put forward by George Stigler (1971).

st.2: Its National Master Plan portal was developed by NITI Aayog.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: the GatiShakti National Master Plan portal was developed by BISAG-N.

st.2: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging NREP and TRYSEM.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: JRY merged NREP and RLEGP; TRYSEM was a self-employment training scheme.

st.2: Average days of work per household rose between 2024-25 and 2025-26.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: average days of work per household fell along with person-days.

st.2: A 'Lakhpati Didi' is an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh a month.
st.3: The Lakhpati Didi target of 6 crore women has already been reached.
st.4: The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) promotes farm-based enterprises.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: a Lakhpati Didi earns at least ₹1 lakh a year. 3 is false: about 2 crore were reached by February 2026; 6 crore is the target for March 2029. 4 is false: SVEP promotes non-farm enterprises.

st.2: The tier of community institutions immediately above the Village Organisation is the Self Help Group.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: the order is SHG, then Village Organisation, then Cluster-Level Federation; the SHG is below the VO.

st.2: It was launched as part of the first DBT pilot on 1 January 2013.
st.3: It is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: PAHAL began in 54 districts in November 2014 and nationally on 1 January 2015, as the first JAM application. 3 is false: it is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
All four statements are correct: stunting fell to 29.3%, underweight barely moved to 31.8%, severe wasting fell to 5.2%, and early breastfeeding rose to 50.1%.

st.2: Under Section 85, the Krishna River Management Board has its headquarters in Telangana and the Godavari River Management Board in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: it is the other way round – the KRMB is located in Andhra Pradesh and the GRMB in Telangana.

st.1: AP's GSDP for 2025-26 is estimated at ₹17.62 lakh crore, making it the largest State economy in South India.
st.3: Swarna Andhra @2047 was released by NITI Aayog in December 2024.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: AP ranks 8th by GSDP, behind Tamil Nadu and Karnataka in the South. 3 is false: Swarna Andhra @2047 is the AP government's vision (GSDP US $2.4 trillion, PCI about US $42,000).

st.3: It reported bank gross NPAs at a multi-decade high.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: it reported bank GNPAs at 2.2%, a multi-decade low.

st.3: From 2026, the Provisional Estimate has been shifted to the last working day of May.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: from 2026 the Provisional Estimate moved from the last working day of May to 7 June.

st.2: The growth rate of 2024-25 was revised down from 7.1% to 6.5%.
st.4: It raised the overall size of GDP by 3-4% over the old series.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: 2024-25 growth was revised up, from 6.5% to 7.1%. 4 is false: the new series cut GDP size by 3-4%.
All three statements are correct: national income has changed structurally across primary, secondary and tertiary activities, while employment stays concentrated in agriculture.

st.2: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS) was headed by Suresh Tendulkar.
st.3: In Andhra Pradesh the informal share of employment is higher in urban areas (62.3%) than in rural areas (45.6%).

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: NCEUS (2004) was headed by Arjun Sengupta. 3 is false: AP's informal share is higher in rural than in urban areas.

st.2: DeLong (2003) placed India's take-off in the 1990s, after the reforms.
st.3: In the view that treats 1991 as the turning point, the growth of the 1980s was sustainable and had nothing to do with the 1991 crisis.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: DeLong placed the take-off in the 1980s, before the 1991 reforms. 3 is false: in that view the debt-fuelled growth of the 1980s ended in the 1991 crisis.

st.2: The UNDP's first Human Development Report (1990) was led by Mahbub ul Haq of India.
st.3: The Antyodaya programme began in Madhya Pradesh in 1977-78.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: Mahbub ul Haq, who led the first HDR, was from Pakistan. 3 is false: Antyodaya began in Rajasthan in 1977-78.

st.1: The first Andhra Pradesh HDR (2007) was prepared by NIRD, Hyderabad, sponsored by the Planning Commission and UNDP.
st.3: Bihar's HDI in 2023 (0.650) was above the national value of 0.685.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: the first AP HDR was prepared by CESS, Hyderabad. 3 is false: Bihar's 0.650 is below the national 0.685.
All three statements are correct: a higher poverty line raises fiscal costs, a lower one excludes the needy, and political sensitivity can delay action on committee reports.

st.2: Cyclical unemployment is the main form of unemployment in India.
st.3: About 90% of India's workforce is in the formal sector.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: India's unemployment is mainly structural (with seasonal and disguised forms), not cyclical. 3 is false: about 90% of the workforce is informal.

st.2: Padma Desai, a critic of India's planned economy, was the first Asian woman to earn a PhD in Economics from Oxford.
st.3: The idea of economic planning in India was derived from the United States.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: her PhD was from Harvard. 3 is false: planning was derived from the USSR.

st.2: DILRMP, ULPIN and NGDRS are initiatives under the labour codes.
st.3: The IBC is classed under labour reforms.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: DILRMP, ULPIN and NGDRS are land-record initiatives. 3 is false: the IBC is not a labour reform; it deals with insolvency and exit.

st.1: Under Article 293(3), a State needs the Centre's consent for any fresh loan, even when no Union loan to it is outstanding.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: Article 293(3) requires consent only while a Union loan (or guaranteed loan) to the State is outstanding.

st.2: Madhya Pradesh has the second-largest share under the 15th FC (2021-26), about 10.058%.
st.3: Uttar Pradesh's share rose under the 16th Finance Commission.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: Bihar has the second-largest share (10.058%). 3 is false: UP's share fell from 17.939% to 17.619% under the 16th FC.

st.2: 5G services in India were first launched by BSNL on 1 October 2022.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: 5G was launched on 1 October 2022 by private operators (Jio, Airtel); BSNL had no 5G then.

st.1: He was the first Governor of the RBI.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor; the first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith.

st.3: The RBI's countercyclical capital buffer, framed in 2015, was activated in 2020.
st.4: The RBI's leverage ratio for D-SIBs is lower than for other banks.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the CCyB framework (2015) has never been activated. 4 is false: D-SIBs face a higher leverage ratio (4%) than other banks (3.5%).

st.2: An SMA-2 account, overdue for 61-90 days, is classified as an NPA.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: SMA-2 is a stressed but standard account; it becomes an NPA only after 90 days.

st.2: Milton Friedman argued that the long-run Phillips curve is horizontal.
st.3: India's Phillips curve is relatively steep, as about 92% of workers are informal.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: Friedman argued the long-run Phillips curve is vertical. 3 is false: with about 92% informal workers India's Phillips curve is relatively flat.

st.2: Revenue deficit is revenue receipts minus revenue expenditure.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts.

st.1: Declarants get immunity under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: FAST-DS 2026 gives immunity under the Black Money Act, not the PMLA.

st.2: It retains the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: the Income-tax Act, 2025 (in force from 1 April 2026) replaces the Assessment Year and Previous Year with a single Tax Year.

st.2: APEDA functions under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
st.3: MPEDA is the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones, while APEDA handles marine products.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: APEDA is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 3 is false: APEDA is the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones and MPEDA handles marine products.

st.2: A tight monetary policy with higher interest rates is an expenditure-switching measure.
st.3: Raising the import duty on gold is an expenditure-reducing measure.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: tight money is an expenditure-reducing measure. 3 is false: a higher import duty switches spending from imports to home goods – an expenditure-switching measure.

st.1: The Agriculture Orientation Index (SDG 2.a.1) is compiled by IFPRI.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: the Agriculture Orientation Index is compiled by the FAO.

st.3: Under the PPV&FR Act, 2001, farmers may sell their farm-saved seed as branded seed.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: farmers may sell farm-saved seed only unbranded.

st.2: Farmer suicides are concentrated mainly in irrigated belts.
st.3: As per ADSI 2023, farm-sector suicides numbered 10,786, and Karnataka had the largest share.
st.4: As per ADSI 2023, Andhra Pradesh accounted for 22.5% of farm-sector suicides.

x: Statement 1 is correct. 2 is false: farmer suicides are concentrated in rain-fed belts. 3 is false: Maharashtra had the largest share (38.5%). 4 is false: 22.5% is Karnataka's share; AP's is 8.6%.

st.2: Regional Rural Banks provide more agricultural credit than cooperative banks.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: cooperative banks provide more agricultural credit than RRBs.

st.2: The first step in setting up a regulated market is the construction of a market yard.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the first step is notifying the market area; the Market Committee and then the yard follow.

st.2: C2 excludes rent on owned land.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: C2 includes the rent on owned land and interest on owned capital.

st.3: The State Advised Price is announced by the CACP for each State.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the SAP is announced by the State governments, not the CACP.

st.1: It covers the entire population of India.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: the NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population (about 81 crore people), not everyone.

st.3: Only about half of AP's 1.44 crore rice cards are Aadhaar-seeded.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: all (100%) of AP's 1.44 crore rice cards are Aadhaar-seeded.

st.1: The Amaravati Economic Region covers more districts than the Visakhapatnam Economic Region.
st.3: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region, a World Bank growth-hub pilot, covers 10 districts.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: Amaravati covers 9 districts, fewer than Visakhapatnam's 10. 3 is false: the Visakhapatnam region is a NITI Aayog growth-hub pilot.

st.1: Its literacy rate (67.35%) is higher than India's.
st.3: Its coastline, officially revised to 1,053.07 km, is the 2nd longest after Gujarat.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: AP's 67.35% is below India's 72.98%. 3 is false: at 1,053.07 km AP is 3rd, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

st.2: The Centre's 100% funding also covers the hydel component.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: the Centre funds only the irrigation component, not the hydel component.

st.1: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor.
st.3: NDB Phase-II roads aim at double-lane links from mandal headquarters to villages.
st.4: APCRDA is the implementing agency of the VCIC.

x: Statement 2 is correct. 1 is false: the VCIC is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor. 3 is false: Phase-II links district headquarters to mandal headquarters. 4 is false: the VCIC is ADB-assisted and implemented by APIIC, not APCRDA.

st.3: The Krishna Zone is chiefly known for coffee and plantation crops.
st.4: The Scarce Rainfall Zone is the State's chief paddy-growing zone.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: coffee belongs to the High Altitude and Tribal Zone, not the Krishna Zone. 4 is false: the Scarce Rainfall Zone grows groundnut and dryland crops.

st.1: Alphonso, mainly from Andhra Pradesh, is the most exported mango variety of India.
st.3: The National Turmeric Board is headquartered at Erode.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. 1 is false: Alphonso comes mainly from Maharashtra (Konkan). 3 is false: the National Turmeric Board is at Nizamabad.

st.1: IDP (4.0) targets 5 lakh first-time jobs in the services sector.
st.2: IDP (4.0) targets 175+ industrial parks, all to be developed only by APIIC.
st.4: The goal of 'One Family, One Entrepreneur' is to be reached by 2047.

x: Statement 3 is correct. 1 is false: the 5 lakh jobs are first-time manufacturing jobs. 2 is false: the 175+ parks include private 'plug and play' parks. 4 is false: 'One Family, One Entrepreneur' is to be reached by 2030.

st.2: A National Institute of Fashion Technology was promised in the Thirteenth Schedule.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the Thirteenth Schedule lists IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, AIIMS, NIDM and others, but no NIFT.

st.2: APTA is the fully State-owned operational arm that runs the Haritha hotels and the Srisailam ropeway.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the operational arm is APTDC; APTA is the nodal tourism authority.

st.2: SIDBI is the nodal agency for recognition of start-ups.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: start-ups are recognised by DPIIT, not SIDBI.

st.1: It merges the SEBI Act 1992, the SCRA 1956 and the Companies Act 2013.
st.4: It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in December 2025.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: it merges the SEBI Act, the SCRA and the Depositories Act 1996, not the Companies Act. 4 is false: it was introduced in the Lok Sabha.

st.4: The Earth–Sun distance remains constant throughout the year.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: the orbit is elliptical, so the distance varies (perihelion in January, aphelion in July).

st.2: Neap tides occur when the Sun and the Moon are at right angles to the Earth.

x: Both statements are correct: spring tides come at new and full moon, and neap tides when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth.

st.3: Pangaea was surrounded by a mega-ocean called the Panthalassa.

x: All four statements are correct: Wegener proposed the theory in 1912, its forces were too weak, Pangaea was ringed by Panthalassa, and the Tethys separated Laurasia from Gondwanaland.

st.2: Tors are residual granite blocks that stand above the weathered surface where joints are widely spaced.
st.3: Block disintegration is the chemical break-up of jointed rock into blocks.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: block disintegration is physical (mechanical) weathering, not chemical.

st.2: Strong tides and currents prevent the formation of a delta.

x: All four statements are correct: deposition builds deltas while strong tides and currents prevent them and keep estuaries open; an estuary is a drowned funnel-shaped mouth and an ecotone.

st.2: The ultimate base level of a river is sea level.

x: All three statements are correct: a graded river has a smooth concave profile, the ultimate base level is sea level (a lake or dam is a local base level), and stream capture works by headward erosion.

st.3: The seasonal shift of the pressure belts is caused by the Earth's rotation rather than by the apparent movement of the overhead Sun.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is false: the belts shift (about 5°–10°) because they follow the overhead Sun, not because of rotation.

st.2: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian States.

x: All three statements are correct: the mainland spans about 8°N–37°N, the Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States, and the 1971–2020 monsoon normal is 868.6 mm.

st.2: Bhutan lies to the north-east of India.
st.3: Afghanistan is a part of the Indian subcontinent.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: Afghanistan is a SAARC member but not part of the Indian subcontinent.

st.4: India is larger in area than Australia.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: India is the seventh largest country, smaller than Australia (sixth).

st.1: Of India's nine neighbours, Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Myanmar touch India only by sea.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: only Sri Lanka and the Maldives touch India only by sea; Myanmar shares a land border.

st.2: The Satpura is a rift valley.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is false: the Satpura is a block mountain (horst); the Narmada and Tapi flow in rift valleys.

st.1: The western coastal plain is broad and emergent.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: the western coastal plain is narrow and submergent.

st.1: The coastal plains of Andhra Pradesh, its 'Rice Bowl', are made of Archaean gneiss.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: the coastal plains are alluvial; Archaean gneiss forms the Rayalaseema plateau.

st.3: On 4 April 2022 the number of districts rose from 13 to 26 under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is false: the 2022 reorganisation into 26 districts was done by the State under its own districts law, not the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

st.4: Horsley Hills (Enugu Mallamma Konda) lie in YSR Kadapa district.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: Horsley Hills lie in Annamayya district (Madanapalle).

st.3: The Chhattisgarh Basin is not much affected by this branch.
st.4: The majority of the monsoon winds enter Tamil Nadu through the Palghat Gap.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: only part of the Arabian Sea branch passes through the Palghat Gap; most of the winds do not enter Tamil Nadu that way.

st.2: Mumbai is moderate while Nagpur is extreme mainly because of distance from the sea.
st.4: India lies wholly between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is false: the Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India; the north lies outside the tropics.

st.2: It gives 48-hour rain forecasts but no flash-flood warnings.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is false: it gives 48-hour rain forecasts and also 6-hour flash-flood warnings.

st.1: It flows west through a rift valley into the Bay of Bengal.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is false: the Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.

st.4: Lime is the main long-term amendment used to reclaim alkaline (sodic) soils.
